en.title: The passé composé
en.goal: Conjugate the passé composé with avoir and with être to talk about past actions.

blocks.title: Passé composé with avoir
blocks.body: The passé composé is the most common tense for talking about the past in French. Most verbs form it with the present tense of avoir + the past participle. Regular -er verbs form the participle by changing -er to -é.

blocks.title: Some irregular participles
blocks.body: Some very common verbs have an irregular participle that you have to memorize — like faire → fait and prendre → pris, two verbs you already know.

blocks.title: Passé composé with être
blocks.body: A small group of verbs (mainly verbs of movement, like aller) and ALL pronominal verbs use être as the auxiliary, not avoir. When the auxiliary is être, the participle agrees in gender and number with the subject — it gets an -e for feminine and an -s for plural.
examples: She went to the market. (être + feminine agreement)
I got up early. (pronominal verb, always with être)
